headline: New law lets employee-owned company retirement plans rely on independent appraisals to value stock that is not publicly traded.
what_it_does: This law covers Employee Stock Ownership Plans (ESOPs), retirement plans where workers build up shares of their employer's stock. When a company's stock is not traded on a public market, the person managing the plan can rely on a value set by an independent appraiser. The appraiser must follow the valuation method laid out in IRS Revenue Ruling 59-60, which lists the factors to weigh when valuing a privately held business.

who_it_affects.group: Workers in employee stock ownership plans at privately held companies
who_it_affects.how: The cash value they receive for their shares when they leave or retire may be based on an independent appraisal done under IRS Ruling 59-60 methods.
They may rely on a qualifying independent appraisal when deciding the fair market value of plan stock that has no public market.

who_it_affects.group: Independent business appraisers and valuation experts
who_it_affects.how: Their valuations can be relied on by ESOP managers only if they follow the methods in IRS Ruling 59-60.
Their stock held in the plan may be valued using a qualifying independent appraisal.
